ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A pure sample of $N_2O_4(g)$ is placed into a rigid, evacuated, 0.500 L container. The initial pressure of the $N_2O_4(g)$ is 760 atm. The temperature is held constant until the $N_2O_4(g)$ reaches equilibrium with its decomposition products. The figure below shows how the pressure of the system changes while reaching equilibrium. By how much will the equilibrium pressure increase if this reaction goes to completion?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure the vertical axis is labeled Pressure (torr), and the horizontal axis is Time. The pressure curve starts from the marked 760 torr, rises with time, and reaches an equilibrium plateau near the marked 886 torr. Then reason: The initial sample is pure N2O4, the container is rigid and the temperature is constant, therefore pressure is proportional to the total amount of gaseous substance. If the reaction N2O4(g) -> 2 NO2(g) goes to completion, every 1 mol N2O4 becomes 2 mol NO2, and the total amount of gaseous substance doubles, so the total pressure at complete reaction is 2 × 760 torr = 1520 torr. The problem asks for the increase from the equilibrium pressure to the complete-reaction pressure, therefore the increase is 1520 torr - 886 torr = 634 torr.

method.method_draft: Use the graph to identify the equilibrium total pressure as 886 torr and the initial pressure as 760 torr. From the text, note that the container is rigid and temperature is constant and the initial sample is pure N2O4. If decomposition goes to completion, N2O4 -> 2 NO2 doubles the total moles, so the completion pressure is 2(760 torr) = 1520 torr. The requested increase from equilibrium to completion is 1520 - 886 = 634 torr.

method.method_draft: From the graph, calculate the equilibrium pressure rise: 886 - 760 = 126 torr. Interpret this rise as the pressure-equivalent extent x of N2O4 decomposition, since the reaction increases gas moles by one per N2O4 decomposed. Thus the pressure-equivalent amount of N2O4 remaining at equilibrium is 760 - 126 = 634 torr. If the reaction then goes to completion, that remaining N2O4 decomposes and adds a net pressure increase equal to 634 torr. Therefore the equilibrium pressure would increase by 634 torr.
